Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

had verb

with a past participle: I had seen

also ’d (had), had done, had been, past perfect, pluperfect

classical

Plin. Ep. 8.20.3: quod nec audieram ante nec vīderam
Liv. 40.21.2: cupīdō eum cēperat in verticem Haemī montis ascendendī

vīderam, fēceram, amāveram

the pluperfect tense: no auxiliary

I had seen, done, loved

What was already done before a moment in the past. Passives and deponents form it with eram: ventum erat, they had arrived. After postquam and ubi Latin usually keeps the perfect where English has “had”. “If I had …” is the pluperfect subjunctive (see would).

Examples

  • quod nec audieram ante nec vīderam, audīvī pariter et vīdī

    what I had neither heard of nor seen before, I heard about and saw at the same momentPlin. Ep. 8.20.3

  • cupīdō eum cēperat in verticem Haemī montis ascendendī

    he had been seized by a longing to climb to the top of Mount HaemusLiv. 40.21.2

  • ad Jāniculum forte ventum erat

    they had happened to reach the JaniculumLiv. 1.34.8

  • Hem, Dēmea, haud aspexeram tē.

    Oh, Demea, I hadn’t seen you.Ter. Ad. 373–374

  • tantum quod mihi nōn dīxerat, quid prīdiē cēnāveram

    the only thing he hadn’t told me was what I’d had for dinner the day beforePetr. 76.1

See also have, would, after.
